newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale head optimistic on sell-off outlook.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale head optimistic on sell-off outlook.

text.p: The chairman of state-owned Aerospatiale said he was optimistic the new French Socialist government would go ahead with a privatisation of the aerospace group planned by the previous conservative administration.

"I am relatively optimistic the privatisation will take place," Yves Michot recently told journalists in southern France. But he said this was his personal opinion and he had no idea of the government's intentions.
A change in Aerospatiale's status was not essential in the short term but would help speed up the pace of European aerospace industry restructuring, he said.

"I note at the moment, for the Anglo-Saxons as well as the Germans, the idea that we can build the European industry of tomorrow with a French partner owned by the state appears difficult for them to imagine," Michot said.

Aerospatiale and its private sector counterparts, British Aerospace Plc (BAe) and Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), are looking at ways to consolidate their civil and defence activities to face up to the U.S. megamergers which are threatening Europe's national companies.
Executives at rival French conglomerate Lagardere say Dasa chose them as partners over Aerospatiale for their missiles and space businesses partly because they were both private-sector companies.
Michot said a privatisation would also be an opportunity to inject badly needed equity capital into Aerospatiale.
Aerospatiale needs about 10 billion francs of share capital to give it a ratio of around 30 percent of equity to turnover, the level which financial analysts were happy with, he said.
That ratio would give Aerospatiale the ability to respond to acquisitions opportunity and to ride out economic downturns.
Aerospatiale finance director Francois Auque said the company has net debt of three billion francs and five billion francs of shareholders capital.

Assuming a planned merger with French combat aircraft maker Dassault Aviation goes ahead, the new Dassault Aerospatiale group will have turnover of 70 billion francs and the extra 10 billion in capital was based on 30 percent of that sales figure.
Auque declined to say how much of Aerospatiale's equity would need to be sold to raise the 10 billion francs.
Michot said that the Dassault merger plan was at an advanced stage and the industrial organisation could be set up quickly once the financial and political decisions were taken.

Under the plan's terms, Dassault would acquire a stake of roughly 20 percent of the new merged group. Aerospatiale executives said details of the merger plan are due to be announced during the Paris Air Show which starts June 14.
The merger plan has not been submitted to the independent Privatisation Commission for approval, Michot said.

The former conservative government had planned to privatise Aerospatiale by the end of this year, after the Dassault merger. The Socialist party had said in its election campaign it was hostile to privatisations.
Michot has said he favours a privatisation along the lines of Cie de Machines Bull, in which industrial companies bought into the capital, including non-domestic investors.
